one_month_reasoning: No SNOW earnings in the window: Q3 FY27 is not yet dated by the company (Q3 FY26 was reported 2025-12-03), so early December, after 2026-10-30. In-window items: (1) the $3.75B 0% convert ($2.0B 2029 at $500.38, $1.75B 2031 at $483.98) closes ~Oct 1; convert-arb short hedging that knocked the stock ~4% around Sep 28 should be mostly spent; (2) two securities cases: the company's MTD in the newer consolidated action is due Oct 13 (a filing, not a ruling), and a ruling on the MTD of the older action's third amended complaint (filed June 3, pending as of Sep 3) could land any time, a small two-sided headline item (the second amended complaint was dismissed with leave in Feb 2026, so dismissal is plausible); (3) hyperscaler Q3 earnings in late October (cloud consumption read-through); (4) Oct 28 FOMC, where hike odds fell to ~36% after the cooler Sep 30 PCE print, so rate risk is smaller than it looked but still two-sided; (5) Form 144 insider sale notice (2026-09-27) adds modest supply. Post-earnings drift from the Sep-2 gap has fully reversed, so no drift edge. With no directional edge I centre on spot $337.50 with ~16% monthly vol (between realized 62%/3.5 = 17.7% and a lower forward vol once the April tariff crash is out of the window). Unchanged from round 1: the supervisor's corrections add no directional information for October.

fair_value.method: Blend of EV/NTM sales (13x ~$9.6B NTM revenue at Sep-2027 -> ~$327), SBC-aware FCF multiple (45x ~$2.5B NTM adj. FCF -> ~$294) and forward P/E (85x ~$3.70 NTM non-GAAP EPS -> ~$315), with ~$1.9B Sep-2027 net cash on ~388M diluted shares; blended ~$314, about 7% below spot.

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: NTM revenue at Sep-2027 ~$9.6B x 13x EV/sales = $124.8B EV + $1.9B Sep-2027 net cash, / 388M diluted shares

inputs_detail.derivation: NTM at Sep-2027 = ~Q4 FY28 + Q1-Q3 FY29. FY28 consensus $8.11B (+28% on ~$6.35B FY27 total revenue from the $6.07B product guide in sources 1-2), with FY29 growth ~25%: ~$9.5-9.8B, take $9.6B (raised from $9.4B after the supervisor showed my 2/3-year roll-forward understated the quarterly build)

Source 7 brackets forward multiples between 12.2x (bear) and 20.5x (bull); stock ~16-17x NTM today. With growth likely mid/high-20s by Sep-2027, GAAP SBC ~27% of revenue and a product gross-margin guide cut to 74% on AI mix (source 21), a skeptic uses the lower-middle, 13x

10-Q Jul-31: cash $1.71B + ST $0.64B + LT $1.98B = $4.33B vs old converts $2.30B face. Add ~$3.71B net new-convert proceeds, less $0.38B capped calls and $0.55B repurchase of in-the-money 2027 notes (retiring only ~$0.26B face): ~$7.1B cash vs ~$5.8B face debt = ~$1.3-1.6B pro forma. Add ~$1.5-1.8B adj. FCF to Sep-2027 less ~$0.65B/yr RSU tax withholding and ~$0.6B/yr buybacks: ~$1.9B
352.8M basic at Jul-31, Q3 non-GAAP diluted guide 382M (incl. ~5M net old-convert excess shares after $225 capped calls); plus ~1.5% net SBC dilution partly offset by buybacks

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM adj. FCF ~$2.5B (26% margin on $9.6B) x 45x = $112B + $1.9B net cash, / 388M

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 guide 23% adj. FCF margin; assume ~3pt expansion by NTM Sep-2027

Bears cite ~40x FCF (55x after SBC/dilution) as already rich (source 4); GAAP SBC $423.6M in Q2 = 27.3% of revenue (10-Q Note 12, source 15) and RSU withholding absorbs a large share of FCF, so no premium above ~45x for a mid/high-20s grower

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM non-GAAP EPS at Sep-2027 ~$3.70 x 85x = ~$315

inputs_detail.derivation: FY28 $3.02 rolled ~2/3 year at ~35% EPS growth (margin expansion from 14.5% op margin guide); Q2 FY27 run-rate $0.62/qtr supports trajectory; not raised despite the higher revenue estimate because the product gross-margin guide was cut to 74% on AI mix (source 21)
Bear writeups cite ~109x forward P/E as excessive (source 4); TIKR model assumes exit P/E ~78.5x (source 8). 85x sits between, still pricing mid-20s growth

bear.story: Consumption slows as AI efficiency and Iceberg/open formats cut storage/compute lock-in; Databricks, now larger than Snowflake at >$7B run-rate growing >80% with its Lakehouse warehousing business at $1.5B+ growing >100% (company PR), takes warehouse share; AI-mix gross-margin pressure (guide cut to 74%) caps margin expansion; product growth slides toward ~20% by FY28 and the multiple compresses to ~9-10x NTM sales. A Databricks IPO would offer a faster-growing public alternative.

base.story: Growth decelerates from 37% to high-20s as comps harden; operating margins expand ~2-3 pts despite gross-margin mix drag; multiple compresses from ~16-17x to ~13-14x NTM sales on ~$9.6B NTM revenue, roughly offsetting revenue growth and leaving the stock near current levels.

bull.story: AI workloads (Cortex, agents) keep product growth in the mid-30s through FY28, NRR climbs past 128%, margin guidance steps up, and the multiple holds ~16-17x; stock approaches the new convert conversion prices (~$484-$500) and top sell-side targets ($500-525).

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$220 (about -35%, ~9x NTM sales) the market would be pricing growth falling to ~20% or lower with NRR sliding toward 115%, i.e. the post-Q2 reacceleration was a one-off, most plausibly because Databricks (>$7B run-rate, >80% growth, warehousing $1.5B+ at >100%) is winning the warehouse workloads. That is a fundamental break rather than 60%-vol noise, though the stock visited $118 in the April 2026 tariff crash, so a macro liquidation can reach this level without a fundamental cause.

reasoning: Round 2 revision. Starting point unchanged: SNOW $337.50 after a violent year (April tariff crash to $118, then Q1/Q2 beats; Q2 FY27 product revenue +37%, FY27 guide $6.07B/+36%, op margin 14.5%, adj FCF 23%, RPO $9.0B, NRR 126%), with the Sep-3 gap fully given back around the $3.75B 0% convert and a Form 144 notice. Supervisor corrections I accept: NTM revenue ~$9.6B not $9.4B (+~$6 on EV/sales); net cash lower because the $548M repurchase buys deep in-the-money 2027 notes (only ~$0.26B face), so pro forma ~$1.3-1.6B and ~$1.9B by Sep-2027 after withholding and buybacks absorb much of FCF; GAAP SBC is 27.3% of revenue, not ~30%; two separate securities cases (MTD due Oct 13 in the newer one; ruling pending on the older one's third amended complaint). On Databricks, the supervisor flagged my SQL '>$1B, >100%' as trade-blog sourced; I traced it to Databricks' own Aug 13, 2026 release, which is stronger: Lakehouse data warehousing $1.5B+ run-rate growing >100%, total >$7B run-rate growing >80%, positive adj. FCF, $190B valuation. That strengthens the competitive bear case (Databricks' warehouse product alone is ~a quarter of Snowflake's size and doubling), so I nudge bear probability up one point. New skeptic evidence: FY27 product gross-margin guide cut to 74% on AI mix, which is why I did not raise NTM EPS despite higher revenue. Revised methods: EV/sales 13x on $9.6B + $1.9B net cash / 388M = $327; FCF 45x on $2.5B = $294; P/E 85x on $3.70 = $315; blend $314 (was $310), ~7% below spot and ~$100 below the ~$414 consensus target (40 analysts, mostly Buy), which I treat as evidence of sentiment not the answer. I disagree mildly with the supervisor's ~$325: my SBC-aware FCF and P/E methods, which it did not weight, sit below the sales method. The 12-month median stays roughly at spot (~$333-338) because ~25-30% revenue growth offsets expected multiple compression; the distribution uses ~45-50% effective vol with a slightly fat left tail. Scenario mean ~$341. One-month: no earnings; neutral around spot. Research was limited to 4 follow-up queries; no option data or priors were used.
